pointers.sentence: The shortcuts are the functions of `django/shortcuts.py`: `render` renders a template into a response, `redirect` makes a redirect to the URL that `resolve_url` finds for an object, a pattern's name or a URL, and `get_object_or_404` and `get_list_or_404`, each with an asynchronous twin, run a query and raise `Http404` when it finds nothing.
The shortcuts are those lines given names (`django/shortcuts.py`).

The parts are kept apart on purpose: loose coupling is one of Django's design philosophies, under which its layers should know of each other only where they must (`docs/misc/design-philosophies.txt`).
The shortcuts relax that rule knowingly, for convenience (`django/shortcuts.py`).

It calls `render_to_string` from the template loader, giving it the request so that the engine's context processors run, and then the response's constructor, with the string, the content type and the status (`django/shortcuts.py:render`, `django/template/loader.py:render_to_string`).

It calls `render_to_string` from the template loader, giving it the request so that the engine's context processors run, and then the response's constructor, with the string, the content type and the status (`django/shortcuts.py:render`, `django/template/loader.py:render_to_string`).

They differ again when the template does not exist: `render` raises in the view, while a `TemplateResponse` is made without complaint, since it has only been told a name, and fails later, when the handler calls its `render` ([The centre of the chain](../handlers/view.md#template-responses)) (`django/template/response.py:SimpleTemplateResponse.render`).

It leaves working out the target to `resolve_url`, and chooses the response class: `HttpResponsePermanentRedirect` if `permanent` is true and `HttpResponseRedirect` if not, with `preserve_request` and `max_length`, the longest `"Location"` the class will accept, passed to it untouched (`django/shortcuts.py:redirect`).
`resolve_url` takes an object, a pattern's name, a view function or a URL under one parameter, and tries them in a fixed order (`django/shortcuts.py:resolve_url`):
The string never reaches the response class, whose test of the scheme would have refused it (`django/urls/base.py:reverse`, `django/http/response.py:HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__`).
The string never reaches the response class, whose test of the scheme would have refused it (`django/urls/base.py:reverse`, `django/http/response.py:HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__`).

If it holds a slash or a dot, `resolve_url` returns it as it stands, as it returns `"gazette.example"` and `"no such/name"` above, so `redirect` given a misspelt name with a dot and no namespace raises nothing and sends the client to the name as a relative URL (`django/shortcuts.py:resolve_url`).

`settings.LOGIN_URL` and `settings.LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL` may each hold a path or a pattern's name, and the code that uses them passes them through this function first (`django/contrib/auth/decorators.py:user_passes_test`, `django/contrib/auth/views.py:LoginView.get_default_redirect_url`).

The generic views do not call it: `SingleObjectMixin.get_object` makes the same translation itself, with a message of its own ([`DetailView` and `ListView`](display.md#detailview-one-object)) (`django/views/generic/detail.py:SingleObjectMixin.get_object`).
The rest of the arguments go to the queryset's `get` (`django/shortcuts.py:_get_queryset`, `django/shortcuts.py:get_object_or_404`).
The rest of the arguments go to the queryset's `get` (`django/shortcuts.py:_get_queryset`, `django/shortcuts.py:get_object_or_404`).

A query that matches several objects raises `MultipleObjectsReturned`, as the search for a headline containing "cat" does above, and the handler, which does not recognise that exception, ordinarily makes a 500 of it ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md#which-exception-becomes-which-response)) (`django/shortcuts.py:get_object_or_404`, `django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

The caller gets every row in memory and no queryset to refine (`django/shortcuts.py:get_list_or_404`).

`aget_object_or_404` awaits the queryset's `aget`, and `aget_list_or_404` builds its list by iterating the queryset asynchronously (`django/shortcuts.py:aget_object_or_404`, `django/shortcuts.py:aget_list_or_404`).
